intended_object: The canonical isomorphism of frames (as an order isomorphism) between the lattice of opens of a space X and the lattice of opens of its soberification. It sends U to {F : F ∩ U ≠ ∅}, and its inverse is the preimage under the unit x ↦ closure{x}. The docstring and the module's soberification construction say this.
explanation: The soberification is the set of (nonempty) irreducible closed subsets of X. Its open sets are exactly the sets {F | F ∩ U nonempty} for U open in X, which is the standard topology. The forward map is `openSet`, which sends U to exactly this set. The inverse map takes the preimage under the unit x ↦ closure{x}. Since closure{x} meets U exactly when x ∈ U, this preimage gives back U. The map is surjective because every open of the soberification has the form `openSet U`. The proofs show it preserves and reflects inclusion. This is the textbook fact that O(X) ≅ O(sob X), in full generality: it holds for any topological space X. I searched this Mathlib version and found no topology on `IrreducibleCloseds` and no soberification construction, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
